keywords.def: a sheltered area of water where ships can safely stop or dock
a person, group, or country competing with another
to create or set up something so it continues to exist
a place that provides access to somewhere else; an important entry point
crossing or relating to the Atlantic Ocean
to officially end a law, system, or practice
an informal settlement, often built on hillsides in Brazil

sentences.en: Today I want to discuss the history of one of the most famous cities in South America: Rio de Janeiro.
sentences.zh: 今天我想聊聊南美洲最著名的城市之一：里约热内卢的历史。

sentences.en: Rio is a city that had become one of the most popular tourist destinations in the world.
sentences.zh: 里约已经成为世界上最受欢迎的旅游目的地之一。

sentences.en: It is known for its colourful carnival celebrations, the Christ the Redeemer statue and white beaches, and of course its association with football and samba music.
sentences.zh: 它以丰富多彩的狂欢节庆祝活动、救世主基督像、洁白的沙滩而闻名，当然，它也与足球和桑巴音乐紧密相连。

sentences.en: Its history is also fascinating! Today I want to discuss how the city got its names, became the centre of battles between European powers, grew into one of the largest slave ports in the world, and at one time was the only city in the America’s to be the capital of a European Empire.
sentences.zh: 它的历史同样迷人！今天我想探讨这座城市是如何得名的、如何成为欧洲列强争夺的中心、如何发展成为世界上最大的奴隶贸易港口之一，以及它曾在一段时间内成为美洲唯一一个欧洲帝国的首都。

sentences.en: We’ll explore how the city built its fortunes based on gold and coffee, and the how the city has developed in the modern period.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨这座城市是如何靠黄金和咖啡发家致富的，以及它在现代时期的发展历程。

sentences.en: And we’ll also practice your English listening comprehension and learn some new vocabulary at the same time!
sentences.zh: 同时，我们也会练习你的英语听力理解，并学习一些新词汇！

sentences.en: Guanabara Bay, where Rio de Janeiro is located, is one of the largest natural harbours in the world.
sentences.zh: 瓜纳巴拉湾是里约热内卢的所在地，也是世界上天然良港之一。

sentences.en: The region is surrounded by mountains, forests, rivers, and lots of land.
sentences.zh: 这个地区四周环山、森林密布、河流纵横，拥有丰饶的土地。

sentences.en: Basically, it has almost everything people need to survive.
sentences.zh: 基本上，它几乎拥有人们生存所需的一切。

sentences.en: And for this reason, people have been settling in the Guanabara Bay area for thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，人们在瓜纳巴拉湾地区定居已有数千年的历史。

sentences.en: The waters were full of fish and shellfish, the forests had animals and plants to eat, and the climate made it possible to grow crops throughout much of the year.
sentences.zh: 这里的水域鱼类和贝类丰富，森林里有可食用的动植物，而且这种气候使得农作物一年中的大部分时间都能生长。

sentences.en: It was a perfect place to live. When Europeans arrived in the early 16th century, the area was already inhabited by indigenous peoples.
sentences.zh: 这是一个绝佳的居住地。当欧洲人在16世纪初抵达时，该地区已经有土著居民居住。

sentences.en: Most of these indigenous peoples spoke languages belonging to the Tupi language family.
sentences.zh: 这些土著居民大多说属于图皮语系的语言。

sentences.en: These people traveled by canoe across the bay, fished in the waters, grew crops such as cassava, and hunted in the surrounding forests.
sentences.zh: 这些人乘独木舟横渡海湾，在水中捕鱼，种植木薯等农作物，并在周围的森林中打猎。

sentences.en: Indigenous influence is still visible in Rio today.
sentences.zh: 在今天的里约，土著的影响依然清晰可见。

sentences.en: For example, many Brazilian place names come from indigenous languages.
sentences.zh: 例如，许多巴西的地名都源自土著语言。

sentences.en: Also, people from Rio are today known as “Cariocas”.
sentences.zh: 此外，里约人今天被称为“卡里奥卡斯（Cariocas）”。

sentences.en: Its exact origin is debated, but most historians agree that this word comes from an indigenous Tupi phrase.
sentences.zh: 它的确切来源众说纷纭，但大多数历史学家认为这个词源于土皮族的土著短语。

sentences.en: Over time, it became the name for the people of Rio de Janeiro.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，它成了里约热内卢人的代名词。

sentences.en: On the 1st of January 1502, a Portuguese expedition sailed into Guanabara Bay.
sentences.zh: 1502年1月1日，一支葡萄牙探险队驶入瓜纳巴拉湾。

sentences.en: They gave the area the name Rio de Janeiro, which literally means “January River.”
sentences.zh: 他们给这个地区取名为里约热内卢，字面意思是“一月之河”。

sentences.en: Interestingly, there wasn’t actually a river there.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，那里其实并没有一条河。

sentences.en: The explorers had entered Guanabara Bay, the large natural harbour but not a river.
sentences.zh: 探险家们进入的是瓜纳巴拉湾这个巨大的天然港口，而不是一条河。

sentences.en: Some of you may have heard the story that the explorers mistook the bay for the mouth of a river, but historians aren’t completely convinced by this.
sentences.zh: 你们有些人可能听说过这样一个故事：探险家们把海湾误认为是河口，但历史学家对这种说法并不是完全信服。

sentences.en: Portuguese sailors were really experienced navigators.
sentences.zh: 葡萄牙水手是非常有经验的航海家。

sentences.en: It’s unlikely they would make such a basic mistake as to confuse a bay with a river.
sentences.zh: 他们不太可能会犯把海湾当成河流这么低级的错误。

sentences.en: Another possibility is that the word “rio”, which now means river, was sometimes used more broadly at the time to describe different types of water.
sentences.zh: 另一种可能是，“rio”这个词现在虽然指河流，但在当时有时被更广泛地用来描述不同类型的水体。

sentences.en: Although Portugal had officially claimed Brazil in the year 1500, it didn’t immediately establish large colonies or cities.
sentences.zh: 尽管葡萄牙在1500年正式宣布对巴西拥有主权，但它并没有立即建立大型殖民地或城市。

sentences.en: That created an opportunity for France, who were one of Portugal’s biggest European rivals.
sentences.zh: 这为法国创造了机会，法国是葡萄牙在欧洲最大的竞争对手之一。

sentences.en: French sailors started to cross the Atlantic to trade with indigenous communities, particularly for a valuable resource called brazilwood.
sentences.zh: 法国水手开始横渡大西洋，与土著社区进行贸易，特别是为了获取一种名为苏木（brazilwood）的宝贵资源。

sentences.en: This tree produced a red dye that was used in Europe for creating luxury textiles.
sentences.zh: 这种树产一种红色染料，在欧洲被用来制作奢侈纺织品。

sentences.en: It was so important that it eventually gave its name to the entire country of Brazil.
sentences.zh: 它如此重要，以至于最终将整个国家的名字赋予了巴西。

sentences.en: The country that produced brazilwood became Brazil.
sentences.zh: 出产苏木的国家成了巴西。

sentences.en: In 1555, a group of French settlers established a colony known as France Antarctique on an island in Guanabara Bay.
sentences.zh: 1555年，一群法国定居者在瓜纳巴拉湾的一个岛屿上建立了一个名为“法属南极”的殖民地。

sentences.en: They hoped to create a permanent French presence in South America.
sentences.zh: 他们希望在南美洲建立一个永久的法国据点。

sentences.en: Portugal, of course, saw this as a serious threat.
sentences.zh: 葡萄牙人当然认为这是个严重的威胁。

sentences.en: In 1565, a military commander known as Estácio de Sá founded a new settlement for Portugal on the edge of the bay.
sentences.zh: 1565年，一位名叫埃斯塔西奥·德·萨的军事指挥官在海湾边缘为葡萄牙建立了一个新的定居点。

sentences.en: He named it São Sebastião do Rio de Janeiro after Portugal’s young king, Sebastian.
sentences.zh: 他以葡萄牙年轻国王塞巴斯蒂安的名字将其命名为圣塞巴斯蒂安-里约热内卢。

sentences.en: Fighting continued for two years between Portuguese forces and the French.
sentences.zh: 葡萄牙军队与法国人之间的战斗持续了两年。

sentences.en: Finally, in 1567, the Portuguese defeated the French and secured control of Guanabara Bay.
sentences.zh: 最终，在1567年，葡萄牙人击败了法国人，确保了对瓜纳巴拉湾的控制。

sentences.en: If France had succeeded, if France had defeated Portugal, Brazil today might be speaking French instead of Portuguese, or perhaps the country would never have become a single nation at all.
sentences.zh: 如果法国人成功了，如果法国人击败了葡萄牙，今天的巴西人可能就会说法语而不是葡萄牙语，或者这个国家可能根本就不会成为一个统一的国家。

sentences.en: But Portugal won, they succeeded, and they are the ones who had control of Brazil.
sentences.zh: 但葡萄牙赢了，他们成功了，他们成为了控制巴西的国家。

sentences.en: For much of its early history, Rio de Janeiro was a relatively modest colonial town.
sentences.zh: 在其早期历史的大部分时间里，里约热内卢只是一个相对较小的殖民城镇。

sentences.en: It was important, but it wasn’t the center of Portuguese Brazil.
sentences.zh: 它很重要，但并不是葡萄牙属巴西的中心。

sentences.en: The center of Portuguese Brazil was Salvador, a city in northeastern Brazil.
sentences.zh: 葡萄牙属巴西的中心是萨尔瓦多，一个位于巴西东北部的城市。

sentences.en: Salvador was an extremely important part of Brazil’s sugar industry.
sentences.zh: 萨尔瓦多是巴西蔗糖产业极其重要的一部分。

sentences.en: Rio slowly developed as a port. The city grew steadily, but there was little reason to think it would become more important than Salvador.
sentences.zh: 里约作为港口缓缓发展。这座城市稳步增长，但当时没什么理由认为它会变得比萨尔瓦多更重要。

sentences.en: Brazil’s sugar industry was the most important part of Brazil’s economy, and Salvador was much closer to the sugar industry than Rio.
sentences.zh: 巴西的蔗糖产业是其经济中最重要的一部分，而且萨尔瓦多比里约更靠近蔗糖产区。

sentences.en: But in the 1690s, Portuguese explorers discovered gold.
sentences.zh: 但在17世纪90年代，葡萄牙探险家发现了黄金。

sentences.en: They discovered gold in a state, a region of Brazil, a few hundred kilometers inland from Rio.
sentences.zh: 他们在距离里约内陆几百公里的巴西一个州、一个地区发现了黄金。

sentences.en: Thousands of gold prospectors rushed into the interior of Brazil.
sentences.zh: 成千上万的黄金勘探者涌入巴西内陆。

sentences.en: These were people searching, mining for gold, and hoping to become rich.
sentences.zh: 这些人寻找并开采黄金，希望能发财。

sentences.en: Historians often compare it to the California Gold Rush of the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 历史学家经常把它与19世纪的加利福尼亚淘金热进行对比。

sentences.en: Vast quantities of gold began to be exported out of Brazil.
sentences.zh: 大量的黄金开始被运出巴西。

sentences.en: Although the gold was located and mined inland, it needed to reach the Atlantic Ocean before it could be shipped to Portugal and then across the world.
sentences.zh: 虽然黄金是在内陆被发现和开采的，但它必须到达大西洋岸边，才能被海运到葡萄牙，然后再运往世界各地。

sentences.en: And Rio became the main gateway for Brazil’s gold exports.
sentences.zh: 里约成为了巴西黄金出口的主要门户。

sentences.en: The gold industry brought wealth into the city.
sentences.zh: 黄金产业给这座城市带来了财富。

sentences.en: More buildings and churches and facilities were built to deal with the growing population.
sentences.zh: 为了应对不断增长的人口，更多的建筑、教堂和设施拔地而起。

sentences.en: As the city became wealthier and more important to the gold industry, more people arrived there, also hoping to become wealthy.
sentences.zh: 随着这座城市变得更加富有、对黄金产业更加重要，更多人涌入这里，同样希望能发财。

sentences.en: In 1763, the Portuguese government moved the capital of colonial Brazil from Salvador to Rio de Janeiro.
sentences.zh: 1763年，葡萄牙政府将巴西殖民地的首都从萨尔瓦多迁至里约热内卢。

sentences.en: Rio was just so much closer to the gold mines.
sentences.zh: 里约距离金矿近得多。

sentences.en: Its location also made it easier to defend the south of Brazil against European powers like Spain.
sentences.zh: 其地理位置也使得防范西班牙等欧洲列强对巴西南部的侵扰变得更加容易。

sentences.en: And Rio’s harbour made it one of the best ports in the entire Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 而且里约的港口使其成为整个大西洋最好的港口之一。

sentences.en: Rio also became dependent on the transatlantic slave trade.
sentences.zh: 里约也变得依赖跨大西洋奴隶贸易。

sentences.en: Between the 16th and 19th centuries, around five million enslaved Africans were brought to Brazil.
sentences.zh: 在16世纪到19世纪之间，大约有五百万被贩卖的非洲黑奴被带到巴西。

sentences.en: Historians estimate that roughly 40% of all Africans transported across the Atlantic arrived in Brazil.
sentences.zh: 历史学家估计，所有横渡大西洋被运送的非洲人中，大约有40%到达了巴西。

sentences.en: Brazil was the number one recipient of African slaves from the transatlantic slave trade.
sentences.zh: 巴西是跨大西洋奴隶贸易中接收非洲奴隶最多的国家。

sentences.en: Many of these slaves passed through Rio de Janeiro.
sentences.zh: 许多奴隶都经由里约热内卢入境。

sentences.en: Rio became one of the busiest slave ports in the world.
sentences.zh: 里约成为了世界上最繁忙的奴隶港口之一。

sentences.en: Ships carrying enslaved people crossed the Atlantic under horrific conditions before arriving at the city.
sentences.zh: 满载奴隶的船只在极其恶劣的条件下拉开大西洋航程，最后抵达这座城市。

sentences.en: The people who survived the journey were sold at markets and forced to work on plantations or in mines.
sentences.zh: 在航行中幸存下来的人在市场上被贩卖，被迫在种植园或矿山劳作。

sentences.en: Enslaved Africans were a major part of the reason that Rio could grow in the way it did.
sentences.zh: 被奴役的非洲人是里约能够蓬勃发展的主要原因之一。

sentences.en: The slaves built roads, unloaded ships in the harbour carried goods through the street, and worked as skilled craftsmen.
sentences.zh: 奴隶们修筑道路、在港口卸货、在街头搬运货物，并充当熟练的工匠。

sentences.en: Slaves also produced the sugar, mined the gold, and later grew the coffee that were the main parts of Brazil’s economy.
sentences.zh: 奴隶们还生产蔗糖、开采黄金，后来又种植了成为巴西经济支柱的咖啡。

sentences.en: Many of the traditions that people now associate with Rio and Brazil have their roots in African cultures.
sentences.zh: 现在人们将里约和巴西联系起来的许多传统，其根源都可以追溯到非洲文化。

sentences.en: Samba is perhaps Brazil’s most famous musical style, and that developed from African rhythms and religious celebrations.
sentences.zh: 桑巴或许是巴西最著名的音乐风格，它就是从非洲节奏和宗教庆典中发展而来的。

sentences.en: Food and religion in Brazil have been influenced by African cultures.
sentences.zh: 巴西的食物和宗教都受到了非洲文化的深刻影响。

sentences.en: And Brazilian Portuguese also contains words and expressions with African origins.
sentences.zh: 巴西的葡萄牙语中也包含许多源自非洲的词汇和表达。

sentences.en: Brazil was one of the last countries in the Western Hemisphere to abolish slavery.
sentences.zh: 巴西是西半球最后一个废除奴隶制的国家之一。

sentences.en: Britain abolished slavery across most of its empire in the 1830s, and the United States abolished it after the Civil War in 1865.
sentences.zh: 英国在19世纪30年代在其大部分帝国境内废除了奴隶制，而美国则在1865年南北战争后将其废除。

sentences.en: But slavery remained legal in Brazil until 1888.
sentences.zh: 但奴隶制在巴西一直合法存在到1888年。

sentences.en: In 1888, former slaves were freed, but most remain trapped in poverty.
sentences.zh: 1888年，前奴隶们获得了自由，但大多数人依然陷入贫困之中。

sentences.en: One of the most fascinating stories in Rio’s history is that it was once the capital of a European empire.
sentences.zh: 里约热内卢历史上最迷人的故事之一，就是它曾是一个欧洲帝国的首都。

sentences.en: Not just the capital of Portuguese Brazil, it was the capital of the Portuguese Empire.
sentences.zh: 它不仅仅是葡萄牙属巴西的首都，而是整个葡萄牙帝国的首都。

sentences.en: It was the only city in the Americas to ever become the capital of a European empire.
sentences.zh: 它是美洲唯一一个曾成为欧洲帝国首都的城市。

sentences.en: It’s really rare for empires to move their capital cities to new continents, new countries.
sentences.zh: 帝国将首都迁往新的大洲、新的国家，这非常罕见。

sentences.en: I can think of the Roman Empire moving their capital to Constantinople or Istanbul today as an example.
sentences.zh: 我能想到的例子是罗马帝国将首都迁往君士坦丁堡，也就是今天的伊斯坦布尔。

sentences.en: But in this case, Rio became the capital of the Portuguese Empire.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，里约成了葡萄牙帝国的首都。

sentences.en: How?
sentences.zh: 怎么会这样呢？

sentences.en: Well, By the early 19th century, Napoleon Bonaparte of France had conquered most of continental Europe.
sentences.zh: 好吧，到了19世纪初，法国的拿破仑·波拿巴已经征服了欧洲大陆的大部分地区。

sentences.en: He demanded that every European country stop trading with Britain.
sentences.zh: 他要求所有欧洲国家停止与英国进行贸易。

sentences.en: But Portugal had been Britain’s closest ally for hundreds of years.
sentences.zh: 但葡萄牙数百年来一直是英国最亲密的盟友。

sentences.en: The two countries depended on each other economically and militarily, and the Portuguese government did not want to abandon their relationship.
sentences.zh: 两国在经济和军事上相互依存，葡萄牙政府不想放弃这种关系。

sentences.en: So Napoleon invaded Portugal. As Napoleon’s troops marched towards Lisbon in late 1807, Portugal’s royal family chose to escape.
sentences.zh: 于是拿破仑入侵了葡萄牙。随着拿破仑的军队在1807年底向里斯本进军，葡萄牙王室选择逃亡。

sentences.en: The British Royal Navy protected a fleet of boats carrying parts of Portugal’s royal family, royal officials, nobles, soldiers, servants, and thousands of other people.
sentences.zh: 英国皇家海军护送着一支船队，船上载有葡萄牙王室成员、皇室官员、贵族、士兵、仆从以及成千上万的其他民众。

sentences.en: They arrived in Rio de Janeiro in 1808. Rio became the capital of the Portuguese Empire.
sentences.zh: 他们在1808年抵达里约热内卢。里约成为了葡萄牙帝国的首都。

sentences.en: No other European monarchy had ever moved its royal court and government to one of its colonies.
sentences.zh: 没有哪个欧洲君主国曾将自己的王室宫廷和政府搬迁到自己的殖民地去。

sentences.en: As it was now home to the empire, the city quickly developed.
sentences.zh: 由于现在成为了帝国的所在地，这座城市迅速发展起来。

sentences.en: The Prince Regent founded the Bank of Brazil, opened libraries and museums, and for the first time allowed a printing press to operate legally in Brazil.
sentences.zh: 摄政王创立了巴西银行，开设了图书馆和博物馆，并首次允许印刷厂在巴西合法运营。

sentences.en: Brazil’s ports were also opened to friendly foreign nations for the first time, which ended Portugal’s monopoly over the colonial trade.
sentences.zh: 巴西的港口也首次对友好的外国开放，这结束了葡萄牙对殖民贸易的垄断。

sentences.en: The Portuguese royal family had intended their stay to be temporary.
sentences.zh: 葡萄牙王室本来打算只是暂住。

sentences.en: Once Napoleon was defeated, they had expected to return to Lisbon.
sentences.zh: 他们曾预计，一旦拿破仑战败，他们就会返回里斯本。

sentences.en: But by the time Napoleon had been defeated, Brazil had become too important and too powerful to just be another colony of Portugal.
sentences.zh: 但等到拿破仑战败时，巴西已经变得太重要、太强大了，不再仅仅是葡萄牙的一个普通殖民地。

sentences.en: When the king eventually returned to Europe, he left behind his son, Dom Pedro On the 7th of September 1822, Dom Pedro made the decision to declare Brazil independent from Portugal.
sentences.zh: 当国王最终返回欧洲时，他留下了他的儿子多姆·佩德罗。1822年9月7日，多姆·佩德罗做出决定，宣布巴西脱离葡萄牙独立。

sentences.en: Unlike many other countries in Latin America, Brazil’s independence was comparatively peaceful.
sentences.zh: 与拉丁美洲的许多其他国家不同，巴西的独立相对和平。

sentences.en: Dom Pedro became Emperor Pedro I, and the new nation was established as the Empire of Brazil, with Rio de Janeiro as its capital.
sentences.zh: 多姆·佩德罗成为佩德罗一世皇帝，新国家建立为巴西帝国，以里约热内卢为首都。

sentences.en: Coffee became the main part of the new empire’s economy.
sentences.zh: 咖啡成为了这个新帝国经济的主体。

sentences.en: It supplied most of the coffee consumed in Europe and North America Immigrants from Portugal, Italy, Germany, Spain, and other countries arrived looking for opportunities.
sentences.zh: 它供应了欧洲和北美消耗的大部分咖啡。来自葡萄牙、意大利、德国、西班牙和其他国家的移民纷纷涌来寻找机会。

sentences.en: Former slaves also moved into the city, hoping to build new lives.
sentences.zh: 曾经的奴隶也搬进了这座城市，希望能重建生活。

sentences.en: Rio became one of the largest cities in the Americas.
sentences.zh: 里约成为了美洲最大的城市之一。

sentences.en: But this meant that many neighborhoods were overcrowded and diseases like yellow fever and smallpox could spread easily.
sentences.zh: 但这意味许多社区过于拥挤，黄热病和天花等疾病极易传播。

sentences.en: In the early 1900s, Mayor Pereira Passos launched a program to renew the city.
sentences.zh: 20世纪初，佩雷拉·帕索斯市长发起了一项改造城市的计划。

sentences.en: He was inspired by the redesign of Paris in the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 他受到19世纪巴黎重新规划的启发。

sentences.en: He ordered hundreds of old buildings to be demolished, replaced narrow streets with broader avenues, improved sanitation, and constructed impressive public buildings.
sentences.zh: 他下令拆毁数百栋老建筑，用更宽阔的大道取代狭窄的街道，改善环境卫生，并建造了宏伟的公共建筑。

sentences.en: He wanted to show Brazil was a modern nation.
sentences.zh: 他想向世人展示巴西是一个现代化的国家。

sentences.en: However, thousands of poorer residents of Rio were forced out of their homes.
sentences.zh: 然而，成千上万的里约贫困居民被迫赶出家园。

sentences.en: Entire neighborhoods had been demolished, and the people living in those neighborhoods had nowhere left to go.
sentences.zh: 整片社区被拆除，住在那些地方的人们无处可去。

sentences.en: There was nowhere affordable to live in the city center.
sentences.zh: 市中心根本没有他们住得起的地方。

sentences.en: Many families had to settle on the surrounding hillsides.
sentences.zh: 许多家庭不得不扎根于周围的山坡上。

sentences.en: They built simple houses wherever they could find space.
sentences.zh: 他们在任何能找到空间的地方搭建简陋的房屋。

sentences.en: These informal settlements gradually became known as favelas.
sentences.zh: 这些非正式定居点逐渐被称为贫民窟（favelas）。

sentences.en: Rio’s magnificent European-style boulevards existed next to hillside slums.
sentences.zh: 里约宏伟的欧式林荫大道与山坡上的贫民窟并存。

sentences.en: Those grand government buildings were next to working-class neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 那些宏伟的政府大楼紧邻着工人阶级社区。

sentences.en: And wealth existed alongside poverty. Rio is, without a doubt, Brazil’s most internationally famous city.
sentences.zh: 财富与贫困并存。毫无疑问，里约是巴西在国际上最著名的城市。

sentences.en: People who’ve never visited Brazil can probably picture Copacabana Beach, or the giant statue of Christ the Redeemer, or Rio’s colorful carnival parades.
sentences.zh: 从未访问过巴西的人大概也能想象出科帕卡巴纳海滩、巨大的救世主基督像，或是里约五彩斑斓的狂欢节游行。

sentences.en: Part of this image comes from Rio’s impressive geography.
sentences.zh: 这种形象部分归功于里约令人叹为观止的地理风貌。

sentences.en: The city is in between mountains and tropical rainforests and the Atlantic Ocean.
sentences.zh: 这座城市夹在山脉、热带雨林和大西洋之间。

sentences.en: In 2012, UNESCO recognized parts of Rio’s landscape as a World Heritage Site.
sentences.zh: 2012年，联合国教科文组织将里约的部分景观认定为世界遗产。

sentences.en: The most famous landmark in the city is the statue of Christ the Redeemer.
sentences.zh: 这座城市最著名的地标是救世主基督像。

sentences.en: I actually recently talked about this statue a few months ago in my episode on the New Wonders of the World.
sentences.zh: 其实我几个月前在关于世界新奇迹的那期节目里刚聊过这个雕像。

sentences.en: And actually, in the bonus episode talking about Other Wonders of the World, I included Guanabara Bay, which had been in CNN’s Natural Wonders of the World list.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在讨论其他世界奇迹的特别节目里，我也把瓜纳巴拉湾收录进去了，它曾登上美国有线电视新闻网的世界自然奇迹名单。

sentences.en: Rio is on two different Wonder of the World lists: Christ the Redeemer as a man-made wonder and Guanabara Bay as a natural wonder.
sentences.zh: 里约登上了两个不同的世界奇迹榜单：救世主基督像是人造奇迹，而瓜纳巴拉湾则是自然奇迹。

sentences.en: Football has also become inseparable from Rio’s identity.
sentences.zh: 足球也已经成为里约身份中不可分割的一部分。

sentences.en: The city is home to legendary Brazilian clubs like Flamengo and Fluminense, Botafogo and Vasco da Gama.
sentences.zh: 这座城市拥有弗拉门戈、弗鲁米嫩塞、博塔弗戈和瓦斯科达伽马等巴西传奇俱乐部。

sentences.en: Rio also has the iconic Maracanã Stadium, which was opened for the 1950 FIFA World Cup and was once the largest football stadium in the world.
sentences.zh: 里约还拥有标志性的马拉卡纳体育场，该球场为1950年国际足联世界杯而建，曾是世界上最大的足球场。

sentences.en: In 1960, Rio lost its status as Brazil’s capital city.
sentences.zh: 1960年，里约失去了巴西首都的地位。

sentences.en: Instead, Brazil officially moved its capital to a brand-new city called Brasília.
sentences.zh: 相反，巴西正式将首都迁往一个名为巴西利亚的全新城市。

sentences.en: If you look at a map of Brazil, almost all of the major cities are located along the Atlantic coast.
sentences.zh: 如果你看一眼巴西地图，就会发现几乎所有的大城市都位于大西洋沿岸。

sentences.en: The government hoped that by building a new capital in the middle of the country, Brasília, they could encourage people and investment to spread across Brazil.
sentences.zh: 政府希望通过在国家中部建立一个新首都——巴西利亚，来鼓励人们和投资向巴西腹地扩散。

sentences.en: Rio remains, the cultural capital of Brazil.
sentences.zh: 里约依然是巴西的文化之都。

sentences.en: When a Hollywood movie wants to show Brazil, it often chooses Rio as the place to represent.
sentences.zh: 当好莱坞电影想要展现巴西时，它通常会选择里约作为代表地。

sentences.en: And when international tourists dream of visiting Brazil, Rio is usually their first destination.
sentences.zh: 当国际游客梦想游览巴西时，里约通常是他们的第一目的地。

sentences.en: The city has also hosted some of the world’s biggest sporting events relatively recently, including the 2014 FIFA World Cup and the 2016 Summer Olympics.
sentences.zh: 这座城市近年来还举办了一些世界最大的体育赛事，包括2014年国际足联世界杯和2016年夏季奥运会。

sentences.en: Today, Rio is one of the most unequal cities in Brazil.
sentences.zh: 如今，里约是巴西贫富差距最大的城市之一。

sentences.en: It has great wealth and middle-class neighborhoods, and also it has neighborhoods suffering with deep poverty.
sentences.zh: 它既有巨大的财富和中产阶级社区，也有深陷贫困之中的社区。

sentences.en: The city’s favelas are often featured in international news coverage, and the news often focuses on crime and poverty.
sentences.zh: 这座城市的贫民窟经常登上国际新闻报道，而新闻往往聚焦于犯罪和贫困。

sentences.en: That’s actually only a small part of the story.
sentences.zh: 这其实只是故事很小的一部分。

sentences.en: More than a fifth, so more than 20%, of Rio’s population lives in favelas.
sentences.zh: 里约超过五分之一、也就是超过20%的人口居住在贫民窟里。

sentences.en: But the vast majority of people living in favelas are ordinary people working and raising families.
sentences.zh: 但绝大多数住在贫民窟里的人都是普通人，他们辛苦工作、养家糊口。

sentences.en: In recent years, many favela residents have worked to change how their neighborhoods are seen.
sentences.zh: 近年来，许多贫民窟居民致力于改变外界对他们社区的看法。

sentences.en: Guanabara Bay has also suffered from decades of pollution caused by untreated sewage and industrial waste.
sentences.zh: 由于未经处理的污水和工业废物，瓜纳巴拉湾也遭受了数十年的污染。

sentences.en: Before the 2016 Olympics, they promised to clean the bay, and although some progress has been made, it’s still not completely clean.
sentences.zh: 在2016年奥运会之前，他们承诺清理这个海湾，尽管取得了一些进展，但它仍然没有完全被清理干净。

sentences.en: Tourism is also a major part of Rio’s economy.
sentences.zh: 旅游业也是里约经济的重要支柱。

sentences.en: Tourism creates jobs, supports restaurants and hotels, and introduces millions of people to Brazilian culture every year.​
sentences.zh: 旅游业创造了就业机会，支持了餐馆和酒店，并每年向数百万人介绍巴西文化。

sentences.en: Rio is a fascinating city. It was the capital of colonial Brazil, then the capital of the Portuguese Empire, and later the capital of an independent Brazilian empire, before eventually giving up that role to Brasilia.
sentences.zh: 里约是一座迷人的城市。它曾是巴西殖民地的首都，然后是葡萄牙帝国的首都，后来又成为一个独立巴西帝国的首都，直到最终将这一角色让给巴西利亚。

sentences.en: It has had big roles in Brazil’s gold and coffee industries.
sentences.zh: 它在巴西的黄金和咖啡产业中发挥过重要作用。

sentences.en: It is a diverse city with African and European influences.
sentences.zh: 这是一座融合了非洲和欧洲影响的多元化城市。

sentences.en: It has great wealth and poverty, and it is located in one of the most beautiful natural landscapes anywhere on the planet.
sentences.zh: 它既有巨额财富，也有贫困，并且坐落在地球上最美丽的自然风景之一中。

sentences.en: As always, I’d love to know what you think.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我很想听听你们的想法。

sentences.en: Have you ever visited Rio de Janeiro? Are you from Rio de Janeiro?
sentences.zh: 你曾经去过里约热内卢吗？你是里约热内卢人吗？

sentences.en: Is it somewhere you would like to visit in the future?
sentences.zh: 这是你将来想去参观的地方吗？

sentences.en: And what city should I look at next in this series?
sentences.zh: 在这一系列节目中，我接下来应该关注哪座城市呢？
